facts.fact: The study states that DHIS2, rolled out by the Ministry of Health as the national reporting system to 112 districts in 2011, is a legacy system managed by the ministry's Division of Health Information; the passage is undated, so the publication date is used.

A census of all 265 government Health Centre IVs, general hospitals, regional and national referral hospitals found DHIS2 available in 100% (265/265) and in use in 98.8% of them; health centre IIIs and IIs were not surveyed, and the survey date is not given in the passages, so the publication date is used.

The study describes paper HMIS registers (maternity, outpatient, inpatient) capturing patient data at user points in the 265 surveyed HC IVs and hospitals, later aggregated and entered into DHIS2, which it calls the system used to capture aggregated data at health facility level; undated in the passages, so the publication date is used.

Among all 265 government HC IVs and hospitals, eAFYA was found in 16.6% (44/265) and the study calls the prevalence of typical EMR systems (eAFYA, Clinic Master, IHMIS) minimal, a ministry informant placing eAFYA and Clinic Master mostly in HC IVs and above; 94.3% (250/265) of facilities kept both paper and digital patient records and 1.9% (5/265) digital only. Survey date not given in the passages, so the publication date is used.

The study states that many of the EMR applications in public facilities (Uganda-EMR, Clinic Master, IHMIS, eAFYA) were deployed by development partners or system vendors to serve their own interests, that facilities rely on implementing partners to support them, and that Uganda lacks national standard guidelines on EMR adoption and use; undated, so the publication date is used.

The study states that the EMR systems in health facilities mostly serve specific programmes and are usually funded by multilateral and bilateral donors, the Government of Uganda being a stakeholder with limited influence, and that implementing partners mostly pay for internet; undated, so the publication date is used.

note: Passages file, read to its end. The study covered HC IV and above only and says it did not investigate HC IIIs and HC IIs, so it gives no clinics figure. Uganda EMR is classed tracker because the study describes it as the HIV/TB programme system. It cites the Health Information and Digital Health Strategic Plan 2020/21-2024/25 and the interoperability guidelines as not fully enforced. Uganda EMR and some EMRs exchange data with DHIS2; interoperability reported in 10% (26/265) of facilities.
